sections.html:
Shreveport is the parish seat of Caddo Parish in northwest Louisiana, on the west bank of the Red River, and part of the city reaches into Bossier Parish. The 2020 census counted 187,593 residents in the city and 393,406 in the Shreveport-Bossier City metro area.

Oil built much of the twentieth century city, and drilling returned later through the Haynesville Shale. Government, health care and education are the biggest employers today, with Barksdale Air Force Base, Caddo Parish Public Schools and Willis-Knighton Medical Center at the top. Many households here depend on the base, the schools or the hospitals, so buyer demand tends to follow those job centers.

Shreveport has a humid subtropical climate, and spring and summer bring severe thunderstorms with hail, damaging wind and tornadoes. Roofs, gutters and tree limbs take the beating.

An older roof with hail marks or patched leaks gets flagged by a conventional buyer's inspector and insurer, and a repair estimate can move a deal. A cash buyer looks at the same roof but prices the work into the offer, so the repair does not hold up the closing.

The city's Department of Property Standards handles abatement of vacant, overgrown and unsafe property. A legal notice the city published in October 2025 shows how the process works and what an owner faces.

  • Owners listed in a notice like that one must fix care of premises, securing and inoperable vehicle violations within 10 days of publication, and demolitions within 30 days.
  • If an owner does not comply, the city can do the work with its own crews or a contractor, and the cost is the owner's responsibility.
  • The city adds an administrative charge of $500 on top of the work, and it may enforce a lien under its ordinance and state law.
  • Environmental Court fines run up to $75 per day per violation on residential property and $300 on commercial property, with a $5,000 cap for residential fines. Owners age 65 and older get an additional 30 days before enforcement.
  • A written appeal is due within 10 days of publication, sent to the Department of Property Standards at P. O. Box 31109, Shreveport, LA 71130.

Anyone acquiring an interest in a listed property is subject to its requirements, so a buyer inherits the problem along with the house. Many of the addresses in such notices are held by estates or unopened successions, which is where a lot of heirs here find themselves.

sections.h2: How Shreveport and Caddo Parish bill property tax
sections.html:
Two bills may apply: one for the parish and one for the city's downtown district if the property sits in it. The Caddo Parish Assessor values the property, and you can reach that office at 318-226-6701. Notices for the city and the Downtown Development Authority (Central Business District) go out in mid-November, with payment due December 31 to the City Finance Department.

The Caddo Parish Sheriff collects parish taxes, also due by December 31. Mailed payments go to PO Box 20905, Shreveport, LA 71120-0905. At closing the title company prorates the year's bill, so ask early whether the current bill has been paid.

sections.h2: What recording a sale costs in Caddo Parish
sections.html:
The Caddo Parish Clerk records deeds, mortgages, rights of way, powers of attorney, judgments and tax liens. Conveyance and mortgage fees run by page count.

DocumentRecording fee
Conveyance or mortgage, 1 to 5 pages$105
6 to 25 pages$205
26 to 50 pages$305
Over 50 pages$305 plus $5 per extra page
Act or affidavit to cancel a mortgage$55
Mortgage certificate, one name and one property$20

An additional $5 fee for the statewide records authority starts January 1, 2027. The record room can help you locate a document but cannot do a title search. Conveyances are indexed back to 1914 and scanned back to 1838.

Heirs make up a large share of the owners who end up with a city notice. A house left behind after a death often sits empty while the family sorts out who owns it, and grass grows and windows go unsecured in the meantime. The city's clock does not wait for the succession.

If that is your situation, gather the death records and any will you have, and see a Louisiana attorney or notary about the succession. Tell any buyer up front that an estate is involved. A buyer who knows early can plan the closing date around the court steps, and a cash buyer will usually take the house with the notices and the grass included in the price.

Keep the tax side moving too. The Sheriff's office and the City Finance Department will each tell you what is owed on the address, and a title company will want both figures before it schedules the act of sale.

sections.h2: When a cash sale makes sense in Shreveport
sections.html:
The situations that tend to fit are an inherited house with open Property Standards notices, a vacant property with grass or securing violations, a house with roof or storm damage, or a rental with long-term tenant problems. In each case the owner wants a firm closing date and a buyer who will take the property as it is.

Title still has to be clear. Sort out any lien from a city abatement, any unpaid tax and any succession questions with a Louisiana notary or attorney before the act of sale. Compare a cash price with what a listing would net after repairs, carrying costs and commissions.

sections.h2: Steps to sell a house that has city notices or back taxes
sections.html:
Start with the paperwork, since most delays here trace back to it. These steps work for a conventional sale and a cash sale alike.

  1. Look up any open Property Standards notice on the address and note the deadlines on it.
  2. Ask the city for the cost of any abatement work it has already done, since that amount can become a lien.
  3. Ask the Sheriff's office and the City Finance Department whether this year's bill has been paid.
  4. Order a mortgage certificate from the clerk, at the fee in the table above, to see what is recorded against the house.
  5. If an owner has died, talk to a Louisiana attorney or notary about whether a judgment of possession is needed before an act of sale can be signed.
  6. Pick the route, listing or cash, and compare what each leaves you after liens, taxes and recording.

A buyer paying cash can skip the appraisal and the lender's repair list, but the title work in steps three and four still happens.

faqs.q: How long do I have to fix a Shreveport property standards violation?
faqs.a: In the city's October 2025 notice, owners had 10 days from publication for care of premises, securing and vehicle violations and 30 days for demolitions. Appeals were due within 10 days.

faqs.q: Can the City of Shreveport put a lien on my house?
faqs.a: Yes. If the city has to do the abatement work, the owner owes the cost plus a $500 administrative charge, and the city can enforce a lien under its ordinance and state law.

faqs.q: When are Caddo Parish property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due by December 31 of the year assessed. City and downtown district notices are mailed in mid-November.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Caddo Parish?
faqs.a: A conveyance of 1 to 5 pages is $105, 6 to 25 pages is $205, and 26 to 50 pages is $305. Fees can change, so confirm with the clerk.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell a Shreveport house before the succession is finished?
faqs.a: Title has to be established first. Talk to a Louisiana attorney or notary about whether a judgment of possession is needed before an act of sale can be signed.
